findings.text: goal_fidelity considered and clean on the axis the section names: re-running the node's own 37-case gate from this review worktree shows a manifest with empty wait fields is not a declared wait and a healthy live worker classifies running, not waiting, wait-aged or unreadable, and the negative half is real -- a genuine declaration (condition, real probe, terminal) still classifies waiting, still ages into wait-aged once the run's stream stops, and is offered to the resume sweep only when its probe reaches a terminal value.

evidence considered, both halves read and the head half re-run: an independent re-run from this review worktree reproduced the recorded head numbers exactly (new file 37 passed; declared cohort 1 failed and 162 passed, the failure being the same pre-existing tests/test_crew_recovery.py::test_refusal_recovery_remedy_survives_promotion at base and head, therefore zero added), while the base side is read rather than re-run and the 7 cases passing at base were not individually enumerated, so the manifest's list of which 7 they are is unverified here.

not considered here: the plan's landed summary and the archive record were read for consistency with the code but not adjudicated claim by claim, and the merged-head result and the full repository suite are outside this node's measure, belonging to a separately dispatched test node.

scope_discipline considered: four of the five declared write paths carry the change as declared and no shared plan, index or sprint state was mutated, but the figure and the archived record are outside the MANIFEST's five declared paths; the reviewed manifest itself discloses the addition in changed_paths and follow_ons, so it is declared scope creep rather than concealment.

durability considered and clean: the manifest block now scopes each of the four wait keys to a wait actually held and dates the orientation write to status in-progress, the reader accepts that word at the reviewed head (reckon/crew/reports.py:80), and the checkpoint scope line the prompt asks for is the one the classifier applies, so prompt and reader cannot disagree about where a non-waiting worker records progress.

fit finding: the new test file adds three findings against the project's declared rule set (ruff on the new file reports exactly three errors -- UP017 at 366 and 398, W292 at 533 -- all autofixable), while base 4df01b3657ba5724900a2b33792f23d7459b3923 and the reviewed head report the same ten findings with the same rule codes for reckon/crew/recovery.py and reckon/crew/prompts.py (B904, FURB162, I001, PERF401, S608, UP017 x3, UP035 x2), so the change adds nothing to the files it edits and three findings in the one it creates.

the prose rule is an open-ended phrase matcher whose stated boundary is narrower than its reach, reproduced by calling the function in-tree: 'none.' reads as a DECLARED wait because the anchor needs whitespace or end-of-string after the word, so a stub spelled with a full stop re-raises the false alarm this change exists to remove, while 'not yet set', 'the job exit status is not yet set' and 'none of the arms have reported yet' read as no wait at all, so a genuine declaration phrased that way is dropped and the worker stays classified running with no wait and no age clock; the captured direction is suppression rather than refusal, so the alarm goes quiet instead of loud, which is the shape of failure this section exists to remove.

the no-op probe rule considered and clean: ['true'], [':'] and ['exit'] are read as no-ops and a real argv such as ['squeue','-h','-j','42','-o','%T'] is kept, matched on the command's basename so '/bin/true' is caught as well.

justifications.durability: Four commits with conventional subjects and bodies on base 4df01b3657ba5724900a2b33792f23d7459b3923 (de8b5e8dca78fd9165a2115af407247ea760132d, 750bc474f3add19e4552d90fc60e591323fa75eb, 0d734fb8d523aba78a174718614e7bf1571a9557, 395450aef98573caadcd50b330130907b7ba3ca6), a clean tree at the reviewed head, and the rule placed in the classifier that reads it with the prompt text moved in step, so a worker is never told a wait the reader will not recognise.
justifications.evidence: The head half was independently re-run from this review worktree (37 passed in 0.46s, and the declared cohort 1 failed and 162 passed with the single failure pre-existing on both sides), the base half was read in full including the tracebacks that show the stub's fields being read as a wait, and the base half was not re-run because checking out the base revision is outside this node's scope.
justifications.fit: The rule reuses the repo's own changed-paths prose-none precedent at promotion.py:706 and the tests follow the file's conventions; the new test file alone adds three lint findings against the declared rule set while the two edited files add none.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The section's outcome holds -- a manifest carrying empty wait fields no longer reads as a declared wait and a healthy worker is never waiting, wait-aged or unreadable -- but the prose rule misses one spelling of the stub and over-matches three plausible genuine declarations, both reproduced against the function at reckon/crew/recovery.py:1125.
justifications.scope_discipline: The five declared paths carry the change, no plan, index or sprint state was mutated, and one artefact -- a figure under docs/figures/crew-observability-truth/ -- sits outside the fence, disclosed by the worker in changed_paths and follow_ons rather than hidden.
